about: Israeli TV exit polls against final results, 2013-2022, per broadcaster. Rows copied on 2026-10-27 from the English Wikipedia 'Opinion polling for the <year> Israeli legislative election' pages (exit-poll rows) and the election results pages. Wikipedia prints one row per broadcaster and does not label it initial (22:00) or updated (around midnight); treat every row as the version Wikipedia recorded, usually the first broadcast. 'bloc' lists the Netanyahu-aligned bloc as each election's table defined it (the Gov./R column). Seats as listed; a row whose listed seats do not sum to 120 is kept as listed and flagged in 'note'. Channel 14 (Channel 20 before 2022) published a party-level exit poll only in 2022. i24NEWS has no party-level exit poll in any table.

elections.note: Kadima shown out by all three, passed with 2; Channel 1 showed Otzma LeYisrael passing, it failed.

exits.note: As listed on Wikipedia the row sums to 116

elections.note: All three understated Likud by 2-3 and overstated the Zionist Union by 2-3; the updated versions moved toward the result during the night.
Channel 12 had Blue and White four ahead and the bloc at 60-60; Channel 13 showed New Right passing (it failed); Channel 13 and Kan showed Ra'am-Balad out (it passed).
The English Wikipedia polling page carries no exit-poll rows for this election and the Hebrew page could not be read in time; left out of the fit rather than filled from memory.
All three gave the bloc 60; it finished 58.

exits.note: As listed on Wikipedia the row sums to 121

elections.note: All three showed Ra'am out; it passed with 4 (the updated versions after midnight brought it in).
All four showed Meretz passing; it failed. The bloc finished 64 against 62 on the three main channels and 61 on Channel 14, whose Religious Zionism figure (12) was the furthest from the result (14).
